description: The complete normalization allowlist. The differ applies these rules, and only these rules, to both the Go and the Rust side before comparing. Every rule cites the Go source of a nondeterminism: Go itself produces different values for the same input, so no exact Go-vs-Rust comparison is possible there. A new rule must cite a Go nondeterminism source, must turn a Go-vs-Go (A/A) self-test diff into zero, and must never hide a Go-vs-Rust difference. Everything not listed here is a mismatch, including everything in not_normalized.

actions.sort: Sort the array at target by the listed keys (stable, ascending, lexical on the JSON text of each key) before comparing.
actions.drop: Remove the member at target on both sides.
actions.key_set: Compare only the set of member names of the object at target, not the values.
actions.shape: Compare only presence and JSON type of the value at target, plus the pattern for strings and the minimum/maximum for numbers; a value outside the shape is compared exactly.
actions.uuid_placeholder: Replace each UUID value at target with <uuid#n>, numbered by first appearance after all sort rules ran, so equal UUIDs stay equal and cross-references are still checked.
actions.count_only: Compare only the count member of a timing value (histogram _count, observation count); ignore sum and buckets.
actions.ignore: Ignore the value at target entirely.
actions.case_insensitive_names: Compare header names case-insensitively and ignore order across different names; the order of values within one name is kept.
actions.candidate_placeholder: Replace a value Go picked by map iteration out of a set of equally valid candidates with a fixed placeholder, only when the value is one of the candidates the trace itself shows and there are at least two of them.

rules.target: $.ext.debug.httpcalls.*[*] (analytics: $[*].object.response.ext.debug.httpcalls.*[*]; the AMP response in http.response and hooks.exitpoint: $.ortb2.ext.debug.httpcalls.*[*]); bidder.result: $.seat_bids[*].http_calls[*]; hooks.all_processed_bid_responses: $.*.http_calls[*]
rules.justification: A bidder with several requests sends them from concurrent goroutines and collects results in completion order. In parity mode the results are collected in call order (fakes.json orders bidder_response_order), but adapters that group imps in a map (ownadx among others) make their requests in map order, so the call order itself differs between Go runs. Every stage that records a bidder's http calls carries that order.

rules.target: $.ext.responsetimemillis (exchange.response: $.ext_bid_response.responsetimemillis); only member values that are non-negative integers are masked
rules.justification: Values are wall-clock elapsed times of each bidder call. A value that is not a non-negative integer (a string, a fraction, a negative number) is compared exactly, because Go never writes one.

rules.target: $.ext.prebid.auctiontimestamp (exchange.response: $.ext_bid_response.prebid.auctiontimestamp; events.tracking: $.auction_timestamp_ms)
rules.justification: Set from the request start time in milliseconds. The shape is a 13-digit millisecond Unix timestamp, so a value in seconds or microseconds is still reported.

rules.target: query parameter ts= of every event URL (bid.ext.prebid.events.*, VAST impression trackers, cached VAST)
rules.justification: Event URLs carry the auction timestamp in milliseconds. The pattern is a 13-digit millisecond Unix timestamp, so a value in seconds or microseconds is still reported.

rules.target: series of the Go runtime collector: go_ followed by one of its families (cgo, config, cpu, gc, godebug, goroutines, info, memory, memstats, sched, sync, threads), after any configured namespace/subsystem prefix
rules.justification: The Go runtime collector reports the process's own memory, GC, scheduler and goroutine state, which changes during every case independently of the request; its runtime/metrics histograms also carry NaN sums.

rules.target: the main listener's connection series connections_opened, connections_closed and connections_error (after any configured namespace/subsystem prefix)
rules.justification: /__parity/exec dispatches the case in process (parity/server/exec.go execute), so no main listener connection belongs to a case. These series count the connections the runner itself holds to the main port, which open on Accept and close when the client or the server's idle timeout (ReadTimeout, no IdleTimeout) ends them, at a moment unrelated to the case: an A/A self-test saw connections_closed move by 1 in about one case in 12000. Connection metrics cannot be compared through exec at all.

rules.target: headers (semantic header comparison only)
rules.justification: Go's http.Header canonicalizes names and has no order across names; the semantic header comparison follows RFC 9110 5.1. Wire-level case and order differences are still reported as kind 'wire' (not_normalized).

rules.target: response header Date
rules.justification: net/http writes the current time into every response.

rules.target: object member order (semantic JSON comparison only)
rules.justification: JSON objects are unordered (RFC 8259); Go sorts map keys and Rust HashMap does not. The lexical comparison of raw bytes still reports member order as kind 'lexical' class 'member_order' (not_normalized).
go_source: encoding/json and jsoniter sort map keys

rules.target: trace.stages.*.*.seq
rules.justification: Session-wide sequence numbers depend on goroutine scheduling across bidders.

rules.target: the gojsonschema error items of a bidder-params validation message, "request.imp[N].ext.prebid.bidder.<bidder> failed validation.\n" followed by "<field>: <description>" items without a separator: request.validated $['@errors'][*].message, the http.response body text ("Invalid request: ...") and the analytics records' error messages. The items are split by the gojsonschema description templates and sorted by (field, description); a list that does not split completely into template items is left as recorded.
rules.justification: gojsonschema validates an object's properties in the order it stored them while parsing the bidder-params schema, and it stores them by ranging over a Go map. PBS parses every schema once at startup, so each process reports the errors of different properties in its own order (two Go processes disagree in about half of the cases with two invalid properties). Which items the message lists, and their text, still compare exactly.

rules.target: the imp ID in "Failed to parse bid mediatype for impression \"<imp>\"" (and the mType variant) in exchange.response $['@errors'][*].message, the http.response body text and the analytics records' error messages. It becomes <stored-auction-imp> only when the side's own stored.responses stage shows at least two imps whose stored auction response holds a bid getMediaTypeForBid rejects (no valid mtype 1-4 and no valid ext.prebid.type), and the reported imp is one of them.
rules.justification: buildStoredAuctionResponse ranges over the stored auction responses by imp ID and returns the first error, so with several failing imps the reported imp is whichever one Go's map iteration reached first. They are masked only when some order of those bids, each overwriting the keys of the bids before it, merges into exactly the recorded targeting.

not_normalized.description: Differences that are never normalized and always gate parity (orchestrator decision). They are reported with their own mismatch kind and class so they can be triaged, but they count against parity/baseline.json like every other mismatch.

classes.header_case: Header name spelling on the wire differs (Go writes canonical case; HTTP/1.1 Go clients send e.g. 'Content-Type').
classes.header_order: Order of different header names on the wire differs.
classes.default_header: A client/server default header differs or is present on one side only (User-Agent Go-http-client/1.1, Accept-Encoding gzip added by Go's transport, Content-Length vs chunked).
classes.http_version: Request or response protocol version differs.
classes.content_length: Content-Length differs or is present on one side only.

classes.html_escape: Go's json.Marshal/jsoniter escape <, > and & as \u003c, \u003e, \u0026 (EscapeHTML true) except where Go disables it (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:386 SetEscapeHTML(false)).
classes.unicode_escape: Other string escapes differ (\u2028, \u2029, invalid UTF-8 replacement, \/).
classes.number_format: Number spelling differs (1 vs 1.0, exponent form, float formatting).
classes.trailing_newline: Encoder.Encode adds a trailing newline that json.Marshal does not (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:391-403).
classes.member_order: Object member order differs in the raw bytes.
classes.unrecorded: One side recorded only the semantic json (no raw, raw_b64, text or b64) of a document the other side recorded as exact bytes, so none of the lexical classes could be checked for it.
classes.other: Any other byte-level difference between semantically equal JSON.

adapter_fakes.description: The 8 adapters with internal randomness or wall-clock reads get deterministic fakes (fakes.json) through branch-only seams; their outputs are compared exactly, never normalized.
